 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The following running back projections highlight what may happen in Week 8 fantasy football. Players are adjusted for matchups, injuries, weather, and much more. Breece Hall's return is expected to be big, while Jonathan Taylor's trade talk adds uncertainty, among many other noteworthy rankings.
 Top-12 Running Backs
 Thomas Carelli
 Jahmyr Gibbs is far above anyone else as the RB1. He is unthreatened at RB in Detroit and almost always gets touches ahead of Sione Vaki. He is also leading all NFL running backs in targets per game.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Breece Hall is an RB1 this week as he returns. As good as Braelon Allen has been, Hall should retain two-thirds of the rushing work, and the Raiders have a bottom-10 run defense. I expect the Jets' offense to perform very well overall.
 In Josh Jacobs' Week 7 return, he had 11 of 17 rushing attempts. That number should continue to rise above 70% of the Packers' team rushing volume.
 High-Upside Running Backs
 Thomas Carelli
 D'Andre Swift is ranked a bit lower than usual, but his ceiling remains slightly high given how good Chicago's offense can be. Swift has at least 14 rushing attempts in any game and 43 over his last two games. If Kyle Monangai stays out, Swift's ranking will move back up.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The game script negatively affected Rhamondre Stevenson's Week 7 output. But in Weeks 4-6, Stevenson averaged 16.3 rushing attempts per game. He is 8th in PFF rushing grade , and the Patriots are expected to take the lead in this game, favoring a run script.
 Bench These Running Backs
 Thomas Carelli
 JK Dobbins is one of the least happy running backs right now. Jonah Coleman's return will eat into Dobbins' workload. In fact, he already did, leading the team in rushing attempts last week with 9, compared with Dobbins' 6.
 TreVeyon Henderson has 13 rushing attempts over his past three games. Corey Kiner has outrushed him in that time, making Henderson barely an outrushed RB2.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Sleeper of the Week
 Seth McGowan does not have an easy matchup. The Jaguars are the NFL's best team in EPA per Rush Allowed. However, I will take a risk here. The Colts have been rumored to potentially sit Jonathan Taylor this Sunday if a trade becomes likely. Regardless, I think the Colts limit Taylor's workload. McGowan could easily lead the Colts in rushing attempts, and the volume alone is noteworthy.
